title: Bayesian optimization and graph learning identify two synthesized ultra-incompressible hard materials
summary: A Bayesian optimization workflow using symmetry-constrained crystal relaxation and the MEGNet graph neural network screened 399,960 transition-metal boride and carbide compositions. The study identified MoWC₂ (P6₃/mmc) and ReWB (Pca2₁), then synthesized both by in-situ reactive spark-plasma sintering; the measured hardness was reported to agree with model and DFT predictions. The result is limited to these two synthesized compounds and the authors’ tested synthesis conditions.
ai_technology: BOWSR (Bayesian Optimization With Symmetry Relaxation) with the MEGNet graph neural network energy model

evidence.tested: A Bayesian optimization workflow using symmetry-constrained crystal relaxation and the MEGNet graph neural network screened 399,960 transition-metal boride and carbide compositions.
evidence.unknown: The arXiv abstract states that the two materials were synthesized and describes them as ultra-incompressible hard materials; the institutional project page reports experiments on eight selected candidates and confirmation of two novel hard materials. The result is from a preprint/journal study and the provided abstract does not give numeric hardness values. Do not imply commercial performance or broader synthesis robustness.
evidence.ai_role: MEGNet supplied graph-based formation-energy predictions; BOWSR used Bayesian optimization under crystal-symmetry constraints to relax candidate structures without DFT geometry relaxation. This enabled screening of 399,960 boride/carbide compositions, narrowing candidates for experimental synthesis.
